# `llm [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...`

Access Large Language Models from the command-line

Documentation: https://llm.datasette.io/

LLM can run models from many different providers. Consult the
plugin directory for a list of available models:

https://llm.datasette.io/en/stable/plugins/directory.html

To get started with OpenAI, obtain an API key from them and:

    $ llm keys set openai
    Enter key: ...

Then execute a prompt like this:

    llm 'Five outrageous names for a pet pelican'

For a full list of prompting options run:

    llm prompt --help

Options:
- `--version`: Show the version and exit.

Default command: `prompt`. When the first argument is not a command name, `llm ARGS...` runs `llm prompt ARGS...`.

Commands:
- `llm aliases`: Manage model aliases
- `llm chat`: Hold an ongoing chat with a model.
- `llm collections`: View and manage collections of embeddings
- `llm embed`: Embed text and store or return the result
- `llm embed-models`: Manage available embedding models
- `llm embed-multi`: Store embeddings for multiple strings at once in the specified collection.
- `llm fragments`: Manage fragments that are stored in the database
- `llm install`: Install packages from PyPI into the same environment as LLM
- `llm keys`: Manage stored API keys for different models
- `llm logs`: Tools for exploring logged prompts and responses
- `llm models`: Manage available models
- `llm openai`: Commands for working with OpenAI and OpenAI-compatible APIs
- `llm plugins`: List installed plugins
- `llm prompt` (default command): Execute a prompt
- `llm schemas`: Manage stored schemas
- `llm similar`: Return top N similar IDs from a collection using cosine similarity.
- `llm templates`: Manage stored prompt templates
- `llm tools`: Manage tools that can be made available to LLMs
- `llm uninstall`: Uninstall Python packages from the LLM environment

Shared options (listed by name in the commands that accept them):
- `-p, --param TEXT TEXT` (repeatable): Parameters for template
- `-o, --option TEXT TEXT` (repeatable): key/value options for the model
- `-T, --tool TEXT` (repeatable): Name of a tool to make available to the model
- `--functions TEXT` (repeatable): Python code block or file path defining functions to register as tools
- `--td, --tools-debug` (env: LLM_TOOLS_DEBUG): Show full details of tool executions
- `--ta, --tools-approve`: Manually approve every tool execution
- `--cl, --chain-limit INT`: How many chained tool responses to allow, default 5, set 0 for unlimited
- `-a, --attachment ATTACHMENT` (repeatable): Attachment path or URL or -
- `--at, --attachment-type TEXT TEXT` (repeatable): Attachment with explicit mimetype, --at image.jpg image/jpeg

Remove an alias

## `llm aliases set [OPTIONS] ALIAS [MODEL_ID]`

Set an alias for a model

Example usage:

    llm aliases set luna gpt-6-luna

Alternatively you can omit the model ID and specify one or more -q options.
The first model matching all of those query strings will be used.

    llm aliases set luna -q gpt-6 -q luna

Arguments:
- `ALIAS` (text; required)
- `[MODEL_ID]` (text)

Options:
- `-q, --query TEXT` (repeatable): Set alias for model matching these strings

## `llm embed-multi [OPTIONS] COLLECTION [INPUT_PATH]`

Store embeddings for multiple strings at once in the specified collection.

Input data can come from one of four sources:

1. A CSV, TSV, JSON or JSONL file:
   - CSV/TSV: First column is ID, remaining columns concatenated as content
   - JSON: Array of objects with "id" field and content fields
   - JSONL: Newline-delimited JSON objects

   Examples:
     llm embed-multi docs input.csv
     cat data.json | llm embed-multi docs -
     llm embed-multi docs input.json --format json

2. A SQL query against a SQLite database:
   - First column returned is used as ID
   - Other columns concatenated to form content

   Examples:
     llm embed-multi docs --sql "SELECT id, title, body FROM posts"
     llm embed-multi docs --attach blog blog.db --sql "SELECT id, content FROM blog.posts"

3. Files in directories matching glob patterns:
   - Each file becomes one embedding
   - Relative file paths become IDs

   Examples:
     llm embed-multi docs --files docs '**/*.md'
     llm embed-multi images --files photos '*.jpg' --binary
     llm embed-multi texts --files texts '*.txt' --encoding utf-8 --encoding latin-1

4. Typed attachments:
   - Each path or URL becomes one embedding
   - Use --at PATH MIME-TYPE to supply an explicit MIME type

   Examples:
     llm embed-multi media -a photo.jpg -a recording.wav
     llm embed-multi media --at recording.data audio/wav

Arguments:
- `COLLECTION` (text; required)
- `[INPUT_PATH]` (file)

Options:
- `--format [json|csv|tsv|nl]`: Format of input file - defaults to auto-detect
- `--files DIRECTORY TEXT` (repeatable): Embed files in this directory - specify directory and glob pattern
- `--encoding TEXT` (repeatable): Encodings to try when reading --files
- `--binary`: Treat --files as binary data
- `--sql TEXT`: Read input using this SQL query
- `--attach TEXT FILE` (repeatable): Additional databases to attach - specify alias and file path
- `--batch-size INT`: Batch size to use when running embeddings
- `--prefix TEXT`: Prefix to add to the IDs
- `-m, --model TEXT` (env: LLM_EMBEDDING_MODEL): Embedding model to use
- `--key TEXT`: API key to use
- `--prepend TEXT`: Prepend this string to all content before embedding
- `--store`: Store the text itself in the database
- `-d, --database FILE` (env: LLM_EMBEDDINGS_DB)
- Shared options: `-a, --attachment`, `--at, --attachment-type`

## `llm openai COMMAND [ARGS]...`

Commands for working with OpenAI and OpenAI-compatible APIs

Commands:
- `llm openai endpoint`: Work with OpenAI-compatible endpoints

## `llm openai endpoint COMMAND [ARGS]...`

Work with OpenAI-compatible endpoints

"llm openai endpoint URL ..." runs the "prompt" subcommand. Use
"add", "list" and "remove" to manage endpoints saved in
extra-openai-models.yaml.

Default command: `prompt`. When the first argument is not a command name, `llm openai endpoint ARGS...` runs `llm openai endpoint prompt ARGS...`.

Commands:
- `llm openai endpoint add`: Save an OpenAI-compatible endpoint to extra-openai-models.yaml
- `llm openai endpoint list`: List endpoints saved in extra-openai-models.yaml
- `llm openai endpoint path`: Output the path to the extra-openai-models.yaml file
- `llm openai endpoint prompt` (default command): Run against an OpenAI-compatible endpoint without logging.
- `llm openai endpoint remove`: Remove a saved endpoint from extra-openai-models.yaml

## `llm openai endpoint add [OPTIONS] URL`

Save an OpenAI-compatible endpoint to extra-openai-models.yaml

The model can then be used with "llm -m MODEL_ID". Example usage:

    llm openai endpoint add https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 \
      -m anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5 --id claude-sonnet \
      --key openrouter --alias claude --supports-tools

If URL is the default OpenAI API URL the api_base key is omitted and
the model uses your regular OpenAI API key.

Arguments:
- `URL` (text; required)

Options:
- `-m, --model TEXT` (required): Model name to send to the API
- `--id TEXT`: Model ID to use with LLM, defaults to the model name
- `--alias TEXT` (repeatable): Alias for the model, can be used multiple times
- `--key TEXT`: Name of a stored key to send to the endpoint, see 'llm keys set'
- `-H, --header TEXT TEXT` (repeatable): Additional HTTP header
- `--responses`: Use the Responses API instead of Chat Completions
- `--completion`: Use the Completions API
- `--supports-tools`: Model supports tool calling
- `--supports-schema`: Model supports JSON schema output
- `--vision`: Model accepts image attachments
- `--audio`: Model accepts audio attachments
- `--reasoning`: Model is a reasoning model
- `--service-tier`: Model supports the service_tier option
- `--no-stream`: Model cannot stream responses
- `--api-type TEXT`: api_type, for Azure OpenAI
- `--api-version TEXT`: api_version, for Azure OpenAI
- `--api-engine TEXT`: api_engine, for Azure OpenAI
- `--replace`: Replace an existing record with the same model ID

## `llm openai endpoint list [OPTIONS]`

List endpoints saved in extra-openai-models.yaml

Options:
- `--json`: Output as JSON

## `llm openai endpoint path`

Output the path to the extra-openai-models.yaml file

## `llm openai endpoint prompt [OPTIONS] URL [PROMPT]`

Run against an OpenAI-compatible endpoint without logging.

PROMPT or stdin is executed once. If neither is provided, wait for
input on stdin. Use --chat to start an interactive chat. Templates run
once by default; use --chat to apply one interactively. Use --models
to list the available model IDs without running a prompt.

Arguments:
- `URL` (text; required)
- `[PROMPT]` (text)

Options:
- `-m, --model TEXT`: Model ID (required unless --models or provided by template)
- `-s, --system TEXT`: System prompt to use
- `-t, --template TEXT`: Template to use
- `--schema TEXT`: Schema DSL, JSON schema, filepath or ID
- `--schema-multi TEXT`: JSON schema to use for multiple results
- `--key TEXT`: API key or stored key alias to send
- `-H, --header TEXT TEXT` (repeatable): Additional HTTP header
- `--responses`: Use the Responses API instead of Chat Completions
- `--chat`: Start an interactive chat
- `--models`: List model IDs from the endpoint and exit
- `--no-stream`: Do not stream output
- `-R, --hide-reasoning`: Hide reasoning output
- Shared options: `-p, --param`, `-o, --option`, `-a, --attachment`, `--at, --attachment-type`, `-T, --tool`, `--functions`, `--td, --tools-debug`, `--ta, --tools-approve`, `--cl, --chain-limit`

Arguments:
- `MODEL_ID` (text; required)

## `llm prompt [OPTIONS] [PROMPT]`

Execute a prompt

Documentation: https://llm.datasette.io/en/stable/usage.html

Examples:

    llm 'Capital of France?'
    llm 'Capital of France?' -m gpt-5.5
    llm 'Capital of France?' -s 'answer in Spanish'

Multi-modal models can be called with attachments like this:

    llm 'Extract text from this image' -a image.jpg
    llm 'Describe' -a https://static.simonwillison.net/static/2024/pelicans.jpg
    cat image | llm 'describe image' -a -
    # With an explicit mimetype:
    cat image | llm 'describe image' --at - image/jpeg

Structured output schemas:

Use --schema to request one JSON object, or --schema-multi to request
multiple objects returned in an "items" array. Both options accept a
concise schema DSL. Define each field as NAME [TYPE]: DESCRIPTION, with
the type and description both optional. Separate fields with commas:

    llm --schema 'name, age int, active bool' 'Invent a dog'

Supported types are str, int, float and bool. The default is str and every
listed field is required. Descriptions provide extra instructions to the
model. Use one field per line if descriptions contain commas:

    llm --schema-multi '
    name: the dog's name
    age int: the dog's age in years
    bio: a short bio, no more than three sentences
    ' 'Invent three dogs'

JSON Schema is also accepted.

The -x/--extract option returns just the content of the first ``` fenced code
block, if one is present. If none are present it returns the full response.

    llm 'JavaScript function for reversing a string' -x

Arguments:
- `[PROMPT]` (text)

Options:
- `-s, --system TEXT`: System prompt to use
- `-m, --model TEXT` (env: LLM_MODEL): Model to use
- `-d, --database FILE`: Path to log database
- `-q, --query TEXT` (repeatable): Use first model matching these strings
- `--options`: Show options for the selected model
- `--schema TEXT`: Schema DSL, JSON schema, filepath or ID
- `--schema-multi TEXT`: Schema for multiple results
- `-f, --fragment TEXT` (repeatable): Fragment (alias, URL, hash or file path) to add to the prompt
- `--sf, --system-fragment TEXT` (repeatable): Fragment to add to system prompt
- `-t, --template TEXT` (repeatable): Template to use; can be repeated to combine templates
- `--no-stream`: Do not stream output
- `-n, --no-log`: Don't log to database
- `--log`: Log prompt and response to the database
- `-R, --hide-reasoning`: Hide reasoning output
- `-c, --continue`: Continue the most recent conversation.
- `--cid, --conversation TEXT`: Continue the conversation with the given ID.
- `--key TEXT`: API key to use
- `--save TEXT`: Save prompt with this template name
- `--async`: Run prompt asynchronously
- `-u, --usage`: Show token usage
- `-x, --extract`: Extract first fenced code block
- `--xl, --extract-last`: Extract last fenced code block
- `--json`: Output the response as JSON, same format as llm logs --json
- Shared options: `-a, --attachment`, `--at, --attachment-type`, `-T, --tool`, `--functions`, `--td, --tools-debug`, `--ta, --tools-approve`, `--cl, --chain-limit`, `-o, --option`, `-p, --param`

## `llm similar [OPTIONS] COLLECTION [ID]`

Return top N similar IDs from a collection using cosine similarity.

Example usage:

    llm similar my-collection -c "I like cats"

Or to find content similar to a specific stored ID:

    llm similar my-collection 1234

Arguments:
- `COLLECTION` (text; required)
- `[ID]` (text)

Options:
- `-i, --input PATH`: File to embed for comparison
- `-c, --content TEXT`: Content to embed for comparison
- `--binary`: Treat input as binary data
- `-n, --number INT` (default: 10): Number of results to return
- `-p, --plain`: Output in plain text format
- `-d, --database FILE` (env: LLM_EMBEDDINGS_DB)
- `--prefix TEXT`: Just IDs with this prefix
- Shared options: `-a, --attachment`, `--at, --attachment-type`

## `llm templates COMMAND [ARGS]...`

Manage stored prompt templates

Default command: `list`. When the first argument is not a command name, `llm templates ARGS...` runs `llm templates list ARGS...`.

Commands:
- `llm templates edit`: Edit the specified prompt template using the default $EDITOR
- `llm templates list` (default command): List available prompt templates
- `llm templates loaders`: Show template loaders registered by plugins
- `llm templates path`: Output the path to the templates directory
- `llm templates show`: Show the specified prompt template

## `llm templates edit NAME`

Edit the specified prompt template using the default $EDITOR

Arguments:
- `NAME` (text; required)

## `llm templates list`

List available prompt templates

## `llm templates loaders`

Show template loaders registered by plugins

## `llm templates path`

Output the path to the templates directory

## `llm templates show NAME`

Show the specified prompt template

Arguments:
- `NAME` (text; required)

## `llm tools COMMAND [ARGS]...`

Manage tools that can be made available to LLMs

Default command: `list`. When the first argument is not a command name, `llm tools ARGS...` runs `llm tools list ARGS...`.

Commands:
- `llm tools list` (default command): List available tools, optionally including tools supported by a model

## `llm tools list [OPTIONS] [TOOL_DEFS...]`

List available tools, optionally including tools supported by a model

Arguments:
- `[TOOL_DEFS...]` (text)

Options:
- `--json`: Output as JSON
- `-m, --model TEXT`: List tools supported by this model
- Shared options: `--functions`

## `llm uninstall [OPTIONS] PACKAGES...`

Uninstall Python packages from the LLM environment

Arguments:
- `PACKAGES...` (text; required)

Options:
- `-y, --yes`: Don't ask for confirmation
